Article 12
Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is in the form of:
a. acts that neglect women within the household scope by a person who is obligated to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to such woman;
b. acts that result in economic dependency by means of restricting and/or prohibiting from engaging in decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of a person; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruises, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.

REGION
REGARDING
PROTECTION
OF WOMEN
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Article 33
(1) In order to coordinate and synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent shall establish a task force, forum, working group or other institution.
(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

CHAPTER IV
PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND EMPOWERMENT
First Part
Prevention of Violence Against Women

Article 5
Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and handling in a confidential manner, whether provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether governmental or non-governmental.

CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 38
(1) The community can participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if they become aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence towards women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.
Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

BEKASI REGENCY YEAR 2020
REGENT OF BEKASI
WEST JAVA PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BEKASI REGENCY
NUMBER 5 YEAR 2020
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY
REGENT OF BEKASI,
a. that women are assets who play a very important role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations so they need to receive protection guarantees from acts of violence and discrimination and need to be empowered so they can actualize their potential optimally;
b. that in order to realize the fulfillment of women's constitutional rights to be free from torture, treatment that degrades human dignity, the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all violence and to improve the quality of life of women, they need to receive protection and empowerment from the regional government of Bekasi Regency;
c. that the implementation of protection of women in Bekasi Regency has not been able to be carried out optimally and is accompanied by violations of women's rights so that a comprehensive regulation is needed to provide direction, foundation, and legal certainty;
d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women;

Article 21
Legal services as referred to in Article 16 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with law enforcement officials, volunteer companions and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
Article 32
(1) The Regional Government, in its efforts to provide and administer the handling of protection services for women victims of violence, shall establish the UPTD PPA.
(2) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under the regional apparatus responsible to the head of the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
(3) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) has the following duties:
 a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;
 b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
 c. coordinating the preparation and presentation of reports regarding women's protection.
(4) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is grouped into the following roles:
 a. health;
 b. psychology;
 c. social-education;
 d. law; and
 e. economy.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions, as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Article 24
Women's empowerment in the health sector
(1) The implementation of health empowerment as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter a is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that oversees health affairs.
(2) The form of empowerment in the health sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of health services to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
 a. Health services during the pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
 b. Pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
 c. Reproductive health services; and
 d. Services and provision of adequate lactation rooms in every Regional Government institution, public facilities and industry.
(4) Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

 a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;

 b. psychology;
 c. social-education;

 e. economy.

b. provision of opportunities for women to hold public office;

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 38

Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 25
(1) Empowerment of women in the field of education as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b is implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.
(2) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capabilities of women.
(3) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes women's empowerment education, skills education and job training.
(4) The organization of formal and non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 27
Empowerment of Women in the field of law as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d is implemented by Regional Apparatus and other related institutions in the form of:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Empowerment of women in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 22
(1) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 16 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment;
(2) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. district/city governments within one provincial territory; and
b. related agencies and institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Article 5
Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and handling in a confidential manner, whether provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether governmental or non-governmental.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Women's empowerment in the health sector

b. that in order to realize the fulfillment of women's constitutional rights to be free from torture, treatment that degrades human dignity, the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all violence and to improve the quality of life of women, they need to receive protection and empowerment from the regional government of Bekasi Regency;
c. that the implementation of protection of women in Bekasi Regency has not been able to be carried out optimally and is accompanied by violations of women's rights so that a comprehensive regulation is needed to provide direction, foundation, and legal certainty;
d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women;

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. (1) Women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of employment as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter e is carried out by Regional Apparatus with authority over labor and other related agencies in the form of:

Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and handling in a confidential manner, whether provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether governmental or non-governmental.

Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is in the form of:
a. acts that neglect women within the household scope by a person who is obligated to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to such woman;

c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruises, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.

WEST JAVA PROVINCE

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY
REGENT OF BEKASI,
a. that women are assets who play a very important role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations so they need to receive protection guarantees from acts of violence and discrimination and need to be empowered so they can actualize their potential optimally;

d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women;

 a. health;
 b. psychology;
 c. social-education;
 d. law; and
 e. economy.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

CHAPTER I

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Article 32

CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 38
(1) The community can participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if they become aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence towards women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.
Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 27

b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Empowerment of women in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 25

(3) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes women's empowerment education, skills education and job training.
